top.line: Map who originates the PHP story's data, give it to the historian, and create original content through interviews and op-eds.
top.para: The PHP site's attribution data shows news makes up 277 of 418 captured sources but originates 5 of 146 statements; organisations, agencies and people originate the rest. The historian should maintain that map with its own visualisations. Our original content already includes our counts, source watch and correction requests, and could grow through interviews and op-eds from people involved.

in-short.line: Map where the data comes from, give it to the historian, and add people's own words.
in-short.para: A new piece of work maps who creates original data and who passes it on. The PHP site already attributes every claim. News is most of what is read but little of what is original. The historian should own this. We are original in our counts, record and analysis, and could be more so with interviews and op-eds.

who.line: Of 146 originations behind 107 attributed statements, news outlets account for 5; organisations, agencies and people the rest.
who.para: Counted at release v0.22.0: 418 captured sources, 277 of them news pages. Organisations originate 79 statements, agencies 27, named people 22, outlets 5. The PHP Foundation, Wiz, CISA and Cloudflare lead. Claims were found relayed 29 times, 11 by the BBC. Relaying is valuable, but this map shows who created the original, and who should be paid.

historian.line: The historian keeps the record, so it should own the originators map, with visualisations and data work.
historian.para: The historian already handles precedent, corrections, context and version history, but has no schedule card and no recorded round since 22 October. Mapping originators against relays over time needs its own visualisations and data work. Other agents, especially the fact-check desk, can contribute, but one agent should maintain it.

original.line: We are already original in our own counts, our source watch, correction requests and analysis.
original.para: Six attributed statements are figures the site counted itself, and one claim is its own. The source watch re-reads 913 pages, has kept 2,946 snapshots and caught silent rewording. Twelve correction requests are drafted, none sent. Pulse, the risk graph and perspective pieces are analysis nobody else has, because nobody else kept the record.

people.line: The most original content is people: interviews with those affected, and op-eds from those involved.
people.para: The site has one interview, the editor's, with answers from voice memos and five questions awaiting a live session. More could follow: interviews recorded as podcasts or video under the Open Security Summit, questions drafted by an agent, and op-eds by maintainers, defenders, publishers and the affected, published under their own names.

exists.line: The attribution, source watch, counts and one interview exist; the historian's map, interviews and op-eds are proposed.
exists.para: Existing: attribution data, the source watch, correction requests, the site's own counts and the editor's interview. Proposed: the historian owning the originators map with visualisations, interviews with affected people, and op-eds from people involved.

limits.line: Counts are the site's own attribution at v0.22.0; relays are undercounted; nobody has been asked yet.
limits.para: A row can name two originators, and attribution is still being filled in. Relays include only those the fact-check desk found in a capture, so the real number is higher. No interview or op-ed has been requested.

sources.line: A voice memo and the PHP site's data at v0.22.0, read on 25 October 2026.
sources.para: The editor's memo of 25 October 2026 and the PHP story site's sources, attribution, entities, source watch, outreach, interview and team data, plus the historian's role file, with related newsroom articles.
